session_3.result:
I added both bulk operations and committed them as `23b0447`. The suite passes (14 tests).

- **`remove_tasks(ids)`** in `tinytasks/api.py` deletes every task whose id is in `ids` and returns how many it removed. Ids that don't exist are ignored.
- **`rm ID [ID ...]`** calls `remove_tasks` and prints `removed N`.

I added API tests for both functions in `tests/test_api.py` and CLI tests for both commands in `tests/test_cli.py`.

session_4.result:
I added both commands, and the full suite passes (18 tests). The work is committed as `16ee334`.

- **`dedupe`** (no arguments): for tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at`. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the first one in the file. It prints `removed N`. Matching is case-sensitive, so "a" and "A" count as different titles.
- **`copy ID`**: creates a task titled `<title> (copy)` with the same `due_at` as the original, and prints `created task N: ...`. If the ID doesn't exist, it prints `no such task`. The new title isn't passed through `normalize_title`, so a copy of an 80-character title will be longer than 80.

The logic is in `dedupe_tasks()` and `copy_task()` in `tinytasks/api.py`. I added tests for both in `tests/test_cli.py`, including a no-duplicates case and a missing-ID case.

`dedupe` also considers archived tasks.
